facts.recording_gap_note: pre-dates the Experimental Recording Standard (2026-07-12); run is from 2026-06-02. No per-seed metric breakdown survives in the flat manifest or the run pack -- only the 2-seed average. Not independently fixable by re-analysis of this run; only by a fresh recorded re-run.
code_confirmed_mechanism: In the gate_active arm, agent.e3._running_variance is set once (script line 333, to train_variance) and NEVER updated again for the rest of the eval episode. The only setter, update_running_variance(), is reached solely via E3Selector.post_action_update() <- REEAgent.update_residue() (ree-v3/ree_core/agent.py:10686); _eval_condition() (experiments/v3_exq_063a_..._rc_gate.py:305-395) never calls agent.update_residue(). So the gate_active arm is NOT dynamically re-evaluated and 'happening to stay low' -- it is frozen low by script construction.

In the gate_ablated arm, the script forces agent.e3._running_variance = commit_threshold + 0.1 = 0.50 (commit_threshold=REEConfig.commitment_threshold=0.40, ree-v3/ree_core/utils/config.py:1107) and agent.e3._committed_trajectory = None immediately before EVERY select_action() call (script lines 342-344), before result.committed is computed for that tick.

Because of this, n_committed_active_stable=1155.5 / n_uncommitted_active_stable=0.0 / n_committed_ablated_stable=0.0 are a tautological readout of the two forced-constant _running_variance regimes the script installs, not an emergent measurement of gate dynamics. C3 ('committed cond has more committed than uncommitted steps') and C4 ('ablated cond has zero committed steps') cannot fail under this construction regardless of whether the R-c gate does anything at all -- both are vacuous non-degeneracy checks.

The R-c readiness gate itself (should_admit_elevation(), the specific mechanism this re-run's title and rationale name as the thing being re-validated) is exercised on EVERY E3 tick in the gate_active arm and on ZERO ticks in the gate_ablated arm -- not 'at most once' vs 'never', a starker asymmetry, because config.heartbeat.beta_gate_bistable is never set by this driver and defaults False (config.py:3296), so select_action() runs the non-bistable LEGACY branch (ree_core/agent.py:9866 'else:'), which re-evaluates _legacy_admit = (should_admit_elevation(...) and _readiness_admits) if result.committed else True on every tick (agent.py:9866-9882), not only on a commit-entry transition. result.committed is computed live from commit_variance = self._running_variance (e3_selector.py:3843); committed = commit_variance < effective_threshold (e3_selector.py:3847), with effective_threshold constant at commitment_threshold=0.40 for this run (BreathOscillator sweep disabled by default, urgency_weight=0.0, goal_state=None -- none of the effective_threshold modulators are armed by this driver, verified). Gate-active: frozen below threshold every tick -> should_admit_elevation fires every tick. Gate-ablated: forced above threshold every tick before select_action runs -> result.committed=False every tick -> the ternary short-circuits to True WITHOUT ever calling should_admit_elevation. Independently red-teamed and CONFIRMED (see red_team block).

current_precision = 1.0 / (self._running_variance + 1e-6) (e3_selector.py:815-817) is the SAME scalar as _running_variance. Forcing _running_variance to a fixed 0.50 in the ablated arm therefore also fixes current_precision at a fixed ~2.0 for the whole episode, an arbitrary operating point unrelated to what the agent's organically-uncommitted precision would be (ARC-029's own what_would_answer cites operating points as low as rv~0.0054 elsewhere in the corpus). The precision-consuming dual-system arbitration path (_arbitrate_dual_system, e3_selector.py:1623) is gated on use_dualsystem_arbitration (default False, not set by this driver) so is NOT exercised here -- the precision confound in THIS run is carried structurally (same scalar, same gate check) rather than through that specific downstream consumer.

The action-generation mechanism itself differs structurally between committed and uncommitted steps (select_action early-return, agent.py:7237-7253): committed steps replay a stored multi-step plan (traj.actions[:, step_idx, :]); uncommitted/ablated steps repeat the single last-chosen action (self._last_action). This IS the intended, in-architecture content of 'commitment' per the claim's own definition, not an incidental confound -- candidate scoring itself (e3.select()) is unconditional on commit state on E3-tick steps.

targets.recommended_evidence_quality_note: [2026-09-14, failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-063a_2026-09-14, GFLAG-0148 adjudication] V3-EXQ-063a PASS (2026-06-02) is CONFOUNDED and its C3/C4 non-degeneracy checks are VACUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION -- re-tag non_contributory (from supports). Two independently sufficient defects, both code-verified and red-team CONFIRMED: (1) OCCUPANCY: the driver never updates agent.e3._running_variance during eval (no update_residue()/post_action_update() call in _eval_condition), so the gate_active arm is frozen committed 100% of eval steps and the gate_ablated arm is forced uncommitted 100% of eval steps by explicit per-tick override BEFORE select_action -- n_committed_active_stable=1155.5 vs n_uncommitted_active_stable=0.0, n_committed_ablated_stable=0.0 are read off the two forced-constant regimes the script installs, not emergent gate behaviour, and the claim's own within-agent two-mode contrast is never reached. (2) PRECISION: current_precision = 1/(running_variance+1e-6) is the same scalar as the ablation target, so forcing running_variance to commit_threshold+0.1=0.50 also pins precision at a fixed ~2.0 in the ablated arm -- structurally the same confound class the 2026-06-03 autopsy used to retag V3-EXQ-630 non_contributory (failure_autopsy_604a-624a-630_2026-06-03). ADDITIONALLY (new to this autopsy): the R-c commit-readiness gate this re-run's own title names as its subject (should_admit_elevation) is exercised on every E3 tick in the gate_active arm and on ZERO ticks in the gate_ablated arm, because beta_gate_bistable defaults False so the legacy re-evaluate-every-tick branch runs (agent.py:9866) and result.committed -- the precondition for calling should_admit_elevation at all -- is forced False every tick in the ablated arm before select_action runs. So the specific R-c mechanism was, in a real sense, never comparably tested across arms either. Do NOT count this PASS as support for ARC-029. ARC-029's other experimental record: EXQ-125 (2 non-superseded runs, weakens/mixed; a 3rd run's own flat manifest reads evidence_direction=superseded and is inactive) and V3-EXQ-227/V3-EXQ-630 (both non_contributory) -- with 063a re-tagged, ARC-029's genuine experimental record has zero surviving supports (claim_evidence.v1.json's current genuine_exp_direction_counts={supports:1(063a),weakens:1} becomes {supports:0,weakens:1} once re-tagged). NOTE (red-team H1): 6 literature entries remain (literature_confidence=0.785) and are untouched by this autopsy -- overall_confidence will not collapse to zero, and the indexer's mechanical conflict_ratio-based demote_to_candidate threshold (build_experiment_indexes.py, needs conflict_ratio>=0.55) will likely NOT fire automatically post-retag (estimated ratio ~0.14). The recommended demotion below is a GOVERNANCE JUDGMENT CALL on the EXPERIMENTAL record specifically (mirroring how this claim was originally promoted candidate->provisional on experimental grounds, per its own status_note), not an automatic index-triggered consequence -- say so explicitly when applying it. Redesign is NOT blocked on new substrate: claims.yaml's own what_would_answer (P1-P3) already specifies the fix using EXISTING levers (MECH-108 BreathOscillator effective_threshold sweep for a threshold-side, precision-invariant mode driver; use_natural_commit_latch_hold for sustained within-run occupancy) -- route to /queue-experiment.

learning_extracted: A same-scalar ablation (forcing a shared commitment/precision variable to a fixed value) cannot isolate 'commitment mode' as a single variable -- it necessarily also pins precision, which is the same second confound class the 2026-06-03 V3-EXQ-630 autopsy found in the across-tick nav_competence axis. This is now confirmed on the within-tick decisiveness axis (R-c gate) too, i.e. the confound is a property of ARC-029's whole ablation-VEHICLE choice (forcing running_variance directly), not of one particular substrate axis.

A per-episode-constant ablation override (applied before every SELECT step, never allowed to vary) makes a C3/C4-style occupancy 'non-degeneracy' check structurally unfalsifiable -- it verifies the override was applied, not that the gate does anything. Future ablation designs for gated/latching mechanisms should manipulate a driver upstream of the gate (here: effective_threshold via MECH-108's BreathOscillator, already implemented) so the gate's own decision logic is genuinely exercised and can genuinely fail the sanity check if the manipulation is not working.

dispositions.name: v3_exq_125a_arc029_committed_mode_redesign
dispositions.disposition: ACTED ON, not dismissed. This driver genuinely exists on disk and was genuinely never queued (confirmed independently: zero '125a' occurrences in ree-v3/experiment_queue.json; matches claims.yaml's own GFLAG-0149 finding). Read in full (ree-v3/experiments/v3_exq_125a_arc029_committed_mode_redesign.py) before finalising routing, per this skill's re-adjudication read rule. VERDICT: this driver does NOT resolve the confound this autopsy identifies and must not be queued as-is. Its redesign only targets EXQ-125's STATISTICAL-POWER defect (2->5 seeds, num_hazards 4->8, hazard_harm 0.02->0.05, majority-rule criteria) -- it uses the IDENTICAL confounded ablation vehicle as 063a ('force agent.e3._running_variance = commit_threshold + 0.1 ... before each SELECT step', same docstring language verbatim), so it inherits BOTH the occupancy-vacuity (P1) and precision (P2) defects this autopsy found. Queueing 125a unmodified would reproduce the same non-degenerate-by-construction non-contributory result, not resolve it. The routing recommendation below is therefore explicitly NOT 'queue 125a' -- it is a fresh redesign (or a substantial amend of 125a) that replaces the running_variance-forcing ablation vehicle with the threshold-side MECH-108 BreathOscillator driver per claims.yaml's own P1-P3 spec, optionally folding in 125a's orthogonal statistical-power fixes (more seeds, higher hazard density) since those remain valid improvements independent of the ablation-vehicle fix.
